target.title: feat: add Twilio RCS channel [AI]
target.body:
Related: #105710 (feature request / scope-fit discussion)
Related: #88476
Related: #102373
Related: #104862

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can send and receive SMS through Twilio today, but SMS cannot carry most of the conversational surfaces OpenClaw is built around: delivery/read receipts, structured rich actions, high-quality media, and a verified branded sender identity. RCS restores those capabilities on a normal phone number while preserving phone-number reach.

Core already encounters real RCS traffic: merged PR #102373 taught the SMS channel to normalize Twilio `rcs:` addresses emitted by RCS-capable Messaging Services. This PR adds the missing first-class sibling channel: `rcs:+E164` targets, RCS webhooks, structured content, persistent delivery/read status, pairing/allowlist access control, and safe coexistence with SMS webhook setups.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an `rcs` channel plugin modeled on the existing SMS channel (#88476), with provider-specific Twilio behavior isolated behind the channel surface. The public channel contract stays provider-neutral (`rcs` id, `rcs:+E164` addressing, pairing policy, status capture), so additional RBM providers can back the same channel later.

The channel provides:

- **Persistent delivery and read receipts.** Twilio status callbacks progress through `sent`, `delivered`, and `read` (`EventType=READ`). Receipts are stored in OpenClaw's shared SQLite plugin state and surfaced on the agent-visible channel status path across Gateway restarts.
- **Structured rich actions.** OpenClaw's portable `MessagePresentation` is translated into Twilio Content API requests sent via `ContentSid` and `ContentVariables`: suggested replies, URL buttons, rich cards, and media. Inbound `ButtonText`/`ButtonPayload` taps route back as normal agent turns. Carousel/list-picker and PHONE_NUMBER actions are not advertised or emitted.
- **Verified sender identity.** RCS Business Messaging supports a vetted branded sender profile instead of an anonymous number, which matters for anti-spoofing, customer trust, and compliance-sensitive business messaging.
- **Canonical webhook hardening.** Replay protection uses OpenClaw's persistent channel replay guard. Signature validation, AccountSid matching, pairing/allowlists, SSRF-guarded loopback forwarding, per-IP and per-sender limits, and no-silent-drop acknowledgement behavior protect the ingress path.
- **Deterministic SMS/RCS coexistence.** `registerPluginHttpRoute` keeps its legacy callable return contract and default no-op-on-conflict behavior for compatibility. An additive `conflictPolicy: "throw"` opt-in lets SMS and RCS fail startup loudly when a required Twilio webhook route is already owned, with both startup orders covered by tests.

The implementation also follows current channel conventions by:

- ignoring blank Twilio environment fallbacks, matching the merged SMS behavior already on main;
- using OpenClaw's shared persistent replay/state primitives instead of plugin-local Maps;
- keeping test helpers private or in test-only files, with no new dead-code baseline suppressions;
- using native guarded HTTP rather than adding the Twilio SDK.

## User Impact

Users can configure a Twilio RCS sender as an OpenClaw channel, send to RCS phone-number targets with suggested replies, URL buttons, cards, and media, receive inbound messages and button taps, and retain delivery/read receipts across restarts. Private deployments can use pairing or allowlists. Shared SMS/RCS deployments fail clearly on unsafe route ownership instead of leaving one channel silently dark.

Docs cover setup, test/launch expectations, shared webhook topology, security controls, capability limits, and the agent-visible receipt surface without claiming carrier/device proof that this branch does not have.

This PR is AI-assisted.

## Dependencies

The new workspace package has one runtime dependency: `zod@4.4.3`, the repo-standard schema library also used by the SMS channel. Its only development dependency is `@openclaw/plugin-sdk` via `workspace:*`. There is no Twilio SDK dependency; provider calls use the existing HTTP/runtime surfaces.

The `pnpm-lock.yaml` change is the new `extensions/rcs` workspace importer. Removing `zod` would make the schema implementation less canonical and would not eliminate the dependency-graph gate: adding the workspace importer itself changes the lockfile. A repository admin/security approval is therefore still required for the exact head if bundled ownership is accepted.

## Evidence

Focused validation on head `e5cda306ce5`, rebased on `upstream/main` `8fc859a26ad`:

- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- `PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 corepack pnpm test extensions/rcs` — **11 files, 95 tests passed**
- `PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 corepack pnpm test extensions/sms/src/gateway.test.ts` — **4 tests passed**
- `PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 corepack pnpm test src/plugins/http-registry.test.ts` — **10 tests passed**
- `node scripts/generate-plugin-inventory-doc.mjs --check` — pass
- `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check` — pass
- focused `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and max-source-LOC checks — pass; RCS production files remain under the new-file ratchet

The focused RCS suite covers rich-content request shapes, Content API create/send-by-ContentSid, inbound button taps, status parsing and persistent receipt storage across runtime restarts, persistent replay behavior, shared-route collision in both startup orders, rollback after partial registration, signature validation, rate limits, and SMS forwarding boundaries. GitHub-hosted CI remains canonical for the heavy repository-wide lanes.

## Real Behavior Proof (redacted)

Existing live-path evidence for the implementation includes:

1. **Signed webhook end-to-end:** valid Twilio HMAC-SHA1 inbound callbacks route to an agent turn; `ButtonText`/`ButtonPayload` taps route as structured inbound turns; forged signatures return HTTP 403 and never dispatch.
2. **Status callbacks:** signed `delivered` and `EventType=READ` callbacks reach the agent-visible receipt surface. The current head additionally persists those receipts in shared SQLite state.
3. **Coexistence mutation proof:** removing the required-route collision guard makes the SMS/RCS collision tests fail; the current head implements the guard as an additive opt-in rather than changing the registrar's return contract.
4. **Live Twilio Content API acceptance:** the exact `twilio/card` body produced by the content builder (title, body, URL action, and quick reply) was accepted by `https://content.twilio.com/v1/Content` with HTTP 201 and then deleted with HTTP 204.

The remaining proof gap is an approved-sender carrier/device run showing outbound rich rendering, inbound interaction/fallback, and a carrier-originated READ callback on the production Twilio flow. This PR does not claim that proof. The request construction, security boundary, routing, persistence, and receipt handling are covered by the focused tests and live API/signature evidence above.
